+
+
+=== Local Attestation
+
+Systems that cannot rely on remote attestation due to unavailable or unstable
+network connectivity may instead use local attestation.
+
+In this model, the TSM produces attestation evidence for a TVM. A local
+verifier appraises this evidence using reference measurements and appraisal
+rules encoded in a TVM Attestation Payload (TAP).
+A TAP is a cryptographically protected data container created by an authorized
+entity. It serves as a local source of truth for attestation and authorization
+decisions and may additionally carry TVM-specific secrets.
+Based on the appraisal outcome and the contents of the TAP, a local key broker
+provisions secrets to the TVM.
+
+During the TVM creation, the TSM should interact with the local verifier to
+authorize TVM execution, providing a TAP supplied by the OS/VMM as part of the
+TVM creation request. During the TVM runtime, the TVM may present an attestation
+result (e.g., an attestation token signed by a verifier) to the local secret
+broker to retrieve the corresponding secrets.
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+The local verifier and secret broker are defined as distinct logical roles to
+support a broad range of deployment models. For example, an implementation may
+realize the secret broker within a TVM, a platform RoT, or an external
+centralized service shared across multiple devices. Other implementations may
+consolidate the local verifier and secret broker roles within the TSM.
+====
+
+==== Properties
+
+Local attestation utilizes one or more of the following properties:
+
+. TVM–Platform Binding: The system verifies that a TVM is authorized to run on
+the platform.
+. TVM Provenance: The system enforces that only TVMs originating from trusted
+entities run on the platform.
+. Policy-enforced Access to Secrets: The system enforces that a secret is accessed
+only when a TVM and platform are in the expected state.
+
+===== TVM–Platform Binding
+
+A CoVE-enabled platform that supports the TVM-platform binding must consist of a
+mechanism to identify the platform, for example via cryptographic keys exposed
+by an implementation-specific mechanism, such as a hardware RoT with
+support for CoVE DICE.
+The creator of a TVM must then be able to link the identity key with the
+hardware and use it to encode the TAP.
+Only the local verifier and local secret broker running on that platform must
+have access to the key that permits them to decode the TAP.
+Access to such key should be linked to the integrity of all TCB elements.
+
+During the TVM creation, the TSM should request the local verifier to authorize
+a TVM execution based on the conditions specified in a TAP. A TVM, which is
+executing, should be then able to retrieve from the local secret broker secrets
+encoded in the TAP using an implementation-specific interface.
+
+===== TVM Provenance
+
+A CoVE-enabled platform that supports the TVM provenance must implement the
+local verifier who restrict what TVMs are allowed to run. There must be an
+implementation-specific mechanism to provide the local verifier with a list of
+public keys of those authorized to sign TVM images for execution on the platform.
+The creator of a TVM must sign the TAP associated with the TVM with a private
+key that corresponds to one of the authorized public keys. During the TVM
+creation, the TSM requests the local
+verifier to check if the TVM is authorized to execute based on the signature
+inside the TAP and the list of authorized public keys. If the signature cannot
+be validated, the local verifier must reject authorization of a TVM execution
+and the TSM must reject its creation.
+
+===== Policy-enforced Access to Secrets
+
+A CoVE-enabled platform that supports policy-enforced access to secrets must
+implement a secret broker that exposes an implementation-specific secret
+retrieval interface to TVMs. The secret broker must authorize every access to a
+secret and checks that it is granted only when the platform and the TVM satisfy
+all conditions defined in TAP.
+
+==== TVM Attestation Payload (TAP)
+The TAP carries information that allows the local verifier to authorize a
+TVM's execution on the platform and the local secret broker to provision a
+TVM with TVM-specific secrets.
+
+The TAP format that consists of five sections: header, lockboxes,
+measurements, attributes, and secrets. The last three sections form a TAP body
+that must be at least integrity protected. The secret section must be additionally
+confidentiality protected. These protections must be provided using a
+symmetric encryption where the corresponding symmetric key is encrypted inside
+lockboxes.
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Format in CDDL"]
+[source,cddl]
+----
+tap-header = bytes .size 6                          ; Semantic structure applied externally (non-CBOR)
+
+tap-measurements-encrypt = COSE_Encrypt1            ; The plaintext is defined as tap-measurements
+tap-attributes-encrypt = COSE_Encrypt1              ; The plaintext is defined as tap-attributes
+tap-secrets-encrypt = COSE_Encrypt1                 ; The plaintext is defined as tap-secrets
+
+tap-body = {
+   0 => tap-measurements / tap-measurements-encrypt,
+   1 => tap-attributes / tap-attributes-encrypt,
+   2 => tap-secrets-encrypt
+}
+
+tap-body-mac = COSE_Mac0                            ; The plaintext is defined as tap-body
+
+tap = (
+   tap-header,
+   tap-lockboxes,
+   tap-body-mac
+)
+----
+
+===== Header
+To support constrained environments, the TAP shall include a 4 bytes aligned,
+6 bytes long header that precedes the payload.
+The header section carries information about the size, version, and encoding of
+the TAP that should be used by a parser to interpret the binary representation
+of the TAP.
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+Including the TAP size in the fixed binary prelude simplifies implementation in
+embedded and constrained environments. In such systems, firmware can determine
+the total size of the TAP payload without inspecting the payload itself,
+which in some encodings like CBOR does not guarantee fixed‑width integer
+representations. This design avoids partial TAP parsing prior to buffer
+allocation and reduces exposure to malformed‑length and resource‑exhaustion
+attacks.
+====
+
+The version field allows future extensions of the TAP format while preserving
+backward compatibility. The `encoding` field enables use of
+implementation-specific encoding format, for example binary, concise binary
+object representation (CBOR), or JavaScript object notation (JSON).
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Header Format (binary)"]
+[source]
+----
+version = 0                          ; Reserved
+         / 1                         ; Version 1
+         / int .ge 2 .le 255         ; Reserved
+
+encoding = 0                         ; Binary format
+         / 1                         ; CBOR format
+         / int .ge 2 .le 255         ; Reserved
+
+Offset | Size | Field
+-------+-------+---------------------
+0      | 4     | Size (uint32 little-endian)
+4      | 1     | Version (0–255)
+5      | 1     | Encoding (0–255)
+----
+
+===== Lockboxes
+The lockboxes section supports use of the same TAP across different platforms
+and enables use of different cryptographic primitives. Each lockbox contains
+the TAP symmetric key (TSK) that is encrypted using an identity key of one of
+the target platforms. Only the local verifier and local secret broker that
+run on the target platform within the expected TCB can access the TSK and thus
+verify the integrity of the TAP body and decrypt the confidential sections.
+
+To construct a TAP, the TVM owner combines the TAP body's sections into a
+single blob and integrity protects them with a cryptographic tag using a freshly
+generated random symmetric key, called the TSK.
+He creates then lockboxes for target platforms by encrypting the TSK with the
+target platform's identity key and stores them in form of a list in the
+`lockboxes` section.
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Lockboxes Format in CDDL"]
+[source,cddl]
+----
+tap-lockbox-name = bstr
+tap-lockbox-value = COSE_Encrypt1
+
+tap-lockbox = {
+   0 => tap-lockbox-name                  ; Platform identifier, e.g., fingerprint
+   1 => tap-lockbox-value                 ; Encrypted TSK
+}
+
+tap-lockboxes = [
+   * tap-lockbox
+]
+----
+
+===== Measurements
+The measurements sections contains the TVM reference integrity measurements.
+In order to expose secrets to a TVM, the TSM must verify that the TVM's
+integrity matches all defined reference measurements for an algorithm selected
+by the TSM. If the `attributes` section is not empty, then the TSM must
+additionally verify all attributes before releasing a secret.
+
+The value stored in a measurement register should represents the result of
+aggregation of multiple integrity measurements combined using a cryptographic
+hash function. Different standards specify what intermediate integrity
+measurements and in which
+order are applied to produce the final value. The tap-measurement-profile
+field allows a TVM creator to distinguish between these standards.
+A CoVE implementation must support at least one of these standards and the TSM
+must ensure that all measurements of supported standards match the reference
+values.
+
+The tap-measurement-layer field allows a TVM creator to specify reference
+measurements for different layers of software on the platform to distinguish
+between measurement registers corresponding to virtualized and non-virtualized
+environments. The TSM must ensure that the integrity of every layer defined in
+the TAP matches the reference values.
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+One of the use cases for introducing the tap-measurement-layer field is to
+additionally constrain the TVM's execution to platform running expected OS/VMM.
+A TVM owner can define reference integrity measurements for the non-virtualized
+(OS/VMM) layer and virtualized (TVM) layer. A CoVE implementation might, for
+example, use then measured boot and a TPM to store integrity measurement of OS/VMM
+and a vTPM to store integrity measurements of a TVM. The layer field provides
+a way to distinguish between these measurements.
+====
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Measurements Format in CDDL"]
+[source,cddl]
+----
+tap-measurement-id = (
+   (0..23)   /                            ; Register's identifier
+   (24..255)                              ; Reserved
+)
+
+tap-measurement-layer = (
+   0         /                            ; Virtualized (TVM)
+   1         /                            ; Non-virtualized (OS/VMM)
+   (2..255)                               ; Reserved to support nested virtualization
+)
+
+tap-measurement-profile = (
+   0         /                            ; CoVE implementation-specific profile
+   1         /                            ; TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile Specification, Level 00 Version 1.06 Revision 52 Family 2.0
+   (2..255)                               ; Reserved
+)
+
+tap-measurement-algorithm = int           ; See https://www.iana.org/assignments/cose/cose.xhtml
+
+tap-measurement-value = bstr
+
+tap-measurement = {
+   0 => tap-measurement-id                ; Measurement register index
+   1 => tap-measurement-layer             ; Measurement layer
+   1 => tap-measurement-profile           ; Measurement profile
+   2 => tap-measurement-algorithm         ; Hash algorithm identifier
+   3 => tap-measurement-value             ; Measurement value
+}
+
+tap-measurements = [
+   * tap-measurement
+]
+----
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+To allow use cases where, for example, secrets are provided to any TVM executing
+on a platform, the TAP format allows the measurements section to be empty.
+====
+
+===== Attributes
+The attributes section contains a set of rules that define the conditions
+under which a TVM can execute and access the secrets. The implementation
+might not support all types of attributes. It must not expose secrets to a TVM,
+if any condition fails. The presence of an attribute that is not supported
+causes the verification condition to fail.
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Attributes Format in CDDL"]
+[source,cddl]
+----
+hardware_serial_number = 0               ; Unique number identifying hardware
+tcb_svn = 1                              ; TCB's secure version number (SVN)
+secure_boot_enabled = 2                  ; Boolean (1=true, 0=false)
+platform_debug_enabled = 3               ; Boolean (1=true, 0=false)
+tvm_debug_enabled = 4                    ; Boolean (1=true, 0=false)
+max_system_uptime = 5                    ; Maximum system uptime in seconds
+firmware_build_time = 6                  ; Firmware build timestamp
+firmware_version = 7                     ; Firmware version
+license_expiration = 8                   ; License expiration timestamp
+
+tap-attribute-key = hardware_serial_number
+                  / tcb_svn
+                  / secure_boot_enabled
+                  / platform_debug_enabled
+                  / tvm_debug_enabled
+                  / max_system_uptime
+                  / firmware_build_time
+                  / firmware_version
+                  / license_expiration
+                  / int .ge 9 .le 65535  ; Reserved range
+
+eq = 0
+ne = 1
+gt = 2
+lt = 3
+ge = 4
+le = 5
+
+tap-attribute-operand = eq / ne / gt / lt / ge / le
+
+tap-attribute-value = bstr
+
+tap-attribute-entry = (
+   tap-attribute-operand                 ; An operand to define how to compare the values
+   tap-attribute-value                   ; The value of the property
+)
+
+tap-attributes = {
+   * tap-attribute-key => tap-attribute-entry
+}
+----
+
+===== Secrets
+The secrets section is a key value pair, where a key is used to retrieve a value
+and a value is a secret. The keys for the key value pairs must be unique.
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+A common deployment pattern is to protect the confidentiality of a TVM image
+at rest by encrypting a TVM's disk with a secret key that a TVM obtains
+during boot following successful attestation. In such a case, the TAP would
+contain a disk encryption secret that a TVM firmware could retrieve from the TSM.
+====
+
+[caption="Figure {counter:image}: ", reftext="Figure {image}"]
+[title= "TAP Secrets Format in CDDL"]
+[source,cddl]
+----
+tap-secret-value = bstr
+
+tap-secrets = {
+   * (0..65535) => tap-secret-value
+}
+----
